text: A wax vesta half burned, found in the mud of the hollow
why: ¶102 states it directly: a half-burned wax vesta, coated with mud, found in the hollow.

text: When the half-burned wax vesta came into the mud of the hollow
why: A plain question about timing. ¶98 has Holmes note that many feet have been in the hollow since Monday night, so the reader has reason to ask when the match got there.

text: Who struck the match found in the mud of the hollow?
why: A plain question about the match just found. The story gives no answer yet, and the wording does not point to one.

text: Who struck the match found in the mud of the hollow? — the man who struck Straker down
id: q.vesta=the man who struck Straker down
why: A possibility the story has given reason to consider: the police theory places the suspect and the trainer in the hollow during the struggle (¶35, ¶46). It is presented as a possibility, not as established fact.

text: Who struck the match found in the mud of the hollow? — someone there before or after that night, unconnected with the crime
id: q.vesta=someone there before or after that night, unconnected with the crime
why: A possibility the story has given reason to consider: ¶62 mentions gypsies camped within a mile of the spot, and ¶98 notes many feet have been there since Monday.
